# Terhia — Grand Beasts

Tabletop module, draft v0.2 (24 September 2026). Companion to the Player's Manual (PM) and Game Master's Guide (GMG), draft v0.3. v0.2 adds *What an emergence leaves* (§2) and register row 22. Built against Terhia-Canon v1.1: Part I (Substrate and Nodes), Part VIII (Ecological Engine), XI.3 (Beast Register), Appendix D (prior Guru-tier events).

**Scope.** What a beast is and how a ground produces one (section 1); rules for running beasts at each tier (section 2); a roll of standing beasts for the twelve homelands, generated by the Part VIII procedure under recorded node ceilings (section 3); tables for rolling more (section 4); a register of every invention, for ratification (section 5). Nothing here changes a rule in the PM or GMG. The GMG's interim rule for beasts (run an unlisted beast on a practitioner block, GMG §7) is superseded by section 2 for beasts and stands for everything else.

**Status against canon.** Canon Appendix R.8 defers a full bestiary and states the constraint: species lists are against the engine's design, because creatures are environmentally produced, not designed. This module contains no species. Every entry is one emergence, on one ground, in one phase, carrying the five XI.3 fields (base animal, biome, moon, node reading, tier) and a designation in the XI.3 form (ground, descriptor, date). Each entry is a candidate XI.3 row and is not canon until entered. Beasts from the Season 1 episodes, when entered from the episode files, take precedence over any row here that shares a ground. The reading of R.8 that permits the module is register row 1, section 5; reject it and the entries stand as worked examples of the generation procedure only.

**Reading order.** Sections 1 and 2 before the first beast scene. Section 3 for the ground the party is on. Section 4 when a ground needs a beast the roll did not give it.

---

## 1. What a beast is

### The formula

Creature = Base Animal × Biome × Moon × Ethos (Canon Part VIII, Creature Generation). Canon states that this is not metaphorical: the four factors shape what emerges. In play the four factors are four questions the GM answers before a beast enters a scene.

1. **Base animal.** An animal of the ground. The beast is that animal with something changed by the substrate. It eats what the animal eats, dens where the animal dens, and fears what the animal fears, except where the change says otherwise. Record it; the August 2026 audit's duplicate ("Kilnback") was a register failure, and a beast without a base animal cannot be checked against a register.
2. **Biome.** The biome of the ground (Canon Part V; nine biomes, with Coastal and Mountain as overlays on top of any biome). The biome selects a row of the grid.
3. **Moon.** The phase at emergence selects the column. The cell is the ambient effect the beast expresses or was produced by. Node activity fixes the tier ceiling: no beast above the node's reading, and no Master tier from a dormant node.
4. **Ethos.** Canon states that the prevailing ethos of the ground shapes what emerges and does not state how. This module expresses ethos as the record: how the ground's institution files and handles the beast. On Rationalist ground (Blue Accord) a beast is a licensed cull, a contract, an invoice. On Devout ground (Gold Crown) it is a parish entry, and a Master-tier beast is, in doctrine, an entry out of order in the Lender's account (Canon Part I, the Crown's reading). On Reverie ground (Green Chimera) it is a docket item, a closure, a hunting claim that moves with the beast's range. The beast's body is the same on any ground; the paper is not (register row 3).

### The grid

The Biome × Moon grid, ratified rows and extension together (Canon Part VIII). The pattern under it: Velquor distorts, Namaris burns or blinds, Orrivane disorients, Saelura stabilizes or heals, Threnis produces apex or dominant fauna.

| Biome | Velquor | Namaris | Orrivane | Saelura | Threnis |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Forest (Deciduous, Evergreen, Taiga inherit) | Geometric growth | Fire spread | Herd agitation | Rapid healing | Apex beast emergence |
| Taiga (own row) | Bog-light; drowned ground | Crown fire | Compass drift | Sap-rise healing | Pack coordination |
| Tundra | Lake-ice anomaly; permafrost heave | Whiteout glare; false suns | Aurora hallucination | Thaw pockets stabilize | Herd-beast emergence |
| Desert | Mirages | Sandstorms | Heat delirium | Oasis stabilization | Burrow dominance |
| Tropical Rainforest | Rot acceleration | Canopy fire (rare) | Swarm disorientation | Rapid healing beyond record | Canopy predator emergence |
| Savanna | Dead-ground avoidance by herds | Grass fire | Migration reversal | Waterhole stabilization | Pride dominance |
| Grassland | Ring necrosis | Wildfire front | Herd agitation | Soil recovery | Burrow and raptor apex |
| Chaparral | Scrub die-off | Firestorm | Heat delirium | Spring resurgence | Ambush predator magnification |
| Coastal (overlay) | Tidal distortion | Storm surge | Migratory disruption | Coral recovery | Reef intelligence |
| Mountain (overlay) | Fault shifts | Avalanche | Echo hallucination | Monastic refuge | Predator magnification |

Taiga has both an inherited Forest row and its own extended row in canon; this module uses the extended row for taiga ground and notes where the Forest row was used instead.

### Tiers

The Grand Beast Tier table (Canon Part VIII), with the rule each column becomes in section 2.

| Tier | Power source | Vulnerability origin | Vulnerability logic | Rule (section 2) |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Novice | Amplified natural trait | Behavioral rigidity | Pattern exploitation | Trait; Rigidity; Exploit |
| Adept | Magical enhancement | Biological dependency | Substrate disruption | Enhancement; Dependency; Disruption |
| Master | Environmental dominance | Energy inversion | Environmental reversal | Dominance; Reversal |
| Guru | Lunar embodiment | Geographic tether | Domain displacement | Domain; Tether; Displacement |

Tier is not size and not species. A hare can be Adept and a bear Novice; the tier is the node's, the animal's is only the shape. A Guru-tier beast is not an animal at all in the way the other three are: it is the moon's signature expressed through a ground, tethered to a node, and the base-animal field is usually a dispute between records (Frostvatn: the parishes say a beast, the households say the lake mother; R.5 #6, not settled).

### The node

The substrate is more responsive at nodes, fixed loci tethered to terrain features (Canon Part I). Node activity is a reading, kept in the Firstday Watch's phase ledgers; it governs what emerges and not what a practitioner pays (decided 11 September 2026). Beast tier cannot exceed the node's reading. A dormant node sustains Novice and Adept emergence and nothing above. Readings across the map have not returned to pre-1218 baseline (Canon Part IX, The Present); every ceiling in section 3 is the Watch's figure for Velquor 1245, and a second record disagrees with it wherever one exists.

### Frequency

How often a tier occurs, stated as the records state it:

- **Novice.** Common. A herder's count, a fire-house tally, a harbor-master's log carries several per phase on any working ground. Most are pests, prizes, or hazards of a season; most are never filed.
- **Adept.** Uncommon. On the order of one per settlement per year, on the Ledger's cull licences for Accord territory; the Concord's dockets carry more, because a Chimera claimant reports what a Ledger examiner would not license.
- **Master.** Rare. Two in the Chronicle since 1145 (Shalei 1155, Mwamba 1186), each a period's largest beast event; this module's roll adds two standing [N]. A Master-tier beast closes a road, empties a valley, or holds a front line; its cull is a phase-scale operation.
- **Guru.** Five Watch entries in the calendar of record (Velquor 1027, Namaris 1062, Threnis 1091, Saelura 1118, Velquor 1230). This module's roll adds one rising [N]. A Guru-tier emergence is a campaign, not an encounter.

### Reading a beast

A beast holds information in layers like anything else (PM §8), and the partition is the point: no single layer returns a beast's vulnerability together with its power. What each layer holds, by tier, is in section 2 under each tier; the general shape is this table. "Nothing here" is a true return.

| Layer | What it returns about a beast |
|:--|:--|
| Plain (Notice) | Size, sign, tracks, the trait as seen; a Rigidity after one full turn of watching (section 2) |
| Structure (Arcane) | Mass and speed; at Adept, the composition of a den, lick, spring, or crust, and whether its reading is where the map says it is; at Master, the beast's next position; at Guru, the two values of a tether that accept editing |
| Life (Nature) | Condition; at Adept, what the body needs — the Dependency, when it is biological; at Master, every animal in the Circle including the ones that came because of the beast; at Guru, the ground's ecology entire, which is how a Domain is read |
| Boundary (Necrotic) | What the beast has killed, when, in what register; a carcass ground or a dead-ground that a beast depends on; nothing about the living beast |
| Intent (Divine) | Nothing here for the beast; fear, calm, or resolve among the people facing it |
| Element (Elemental) | The cell where it is elemental: the fire line, the water table, the wind, the ground's stability; where the cell goes next turn; at Guru, the Domain's weather |
| Make (Light / Dark) | Nothing here, unless the beast has been dosed, baited with a bench product, or is a bond |
| Field — Weight | Whether the beast commits this turn, and to what |
| Field — Geometry | Where it will come through; the corridor a herd or pack takes |
| Field — Ground | Distance, cover, the approach; a trail's age (*Track*) |
| Field — Seams | Where a burrow, a nest, a lodge, a crust, or a carapace breaks |
| Field — Nerve | Whether it holds or breaks this turn — the one Field that reads the beast itself |

## 2. Running beasts

### Blocks

Calibrated against the practitioner blocks (GMG §7): a beast of a tier is a fight for a practitioner of the same rank, with the tier's rule on top. Each entry in section 3 lists its own numbers; these are the defaults an entry deviates from.

| Tier | Rank Die | Guard | Vigor | Attack | Damage (natural weapon) | Move |
|:--|:-:|:-:|:-:|:--|:--|:-:|
| Novice | d4 | 12 | 12 | +1 + d4 | d6 + 1 + Rank Die | 8 |
| Adept | d6 | 14 | 18 | +2 + d6 | d8 + 2 + Rank Die | 8 |
| Master | d8 | 16 (18 in Dominance) | 26 | +3 + d8 | d10 + 3 + Rank Die | 10 |
| Guru | — | — | — | — | — | — |

A Guru tier has no block: Domain, Tether, and Displacement (below) are its whole entry.

A beast's Rank Die is added to its attacks, its damage, and any check of the trait, enhancement, or dominance its entry names, in the way a practitioner's Rank Die is added to school work. It is not added to other checks. Beasts do not carry Strain or Marks: a beast's power is paid for by the ground (its trait, its dependency, its domain), not by its body, and the tier's vulnerability rule is where the bill is presented.

Size adjustments, applied by the entry: small (a hare, a viper, a bat) — Guard +2, Vigor halved, damage die one step down; large (an ox, a bear, a bull camel) — Guard −1, Vigor +6, damage die one step up. Two or more beasts of one entry act on one initiative.

### Novice — Trait, Rigidity, Exploit

- **Amplified trait.** One natural trait raised past the animal's range: speed, concealment, endurance, a bite, a display, footing, a coat. Each entry states it as a rule. The trait is always on.
- **Rigidity.** One pattern the beast cannot vary: a route, an hour, a target, a return, a refusal. It is the vulnerability, and it is an animal's, not a flaw designed in.
- **Pattern exploitation.** The Rigidity is *known* when any of these is true: a record in the party's hands states it; a reading returns it (Plain by Notice at Difficulty 13 after one full turn of watching; Field — Weight or Nerve at Novice grade; Life at Novice grade for a feeding or a return); or the beast has shown it twice in the scene. Once known, every check that uses the pattern against the beast has Favor, and the entry's **Exploit** is available: a way to end the encounter without a kill, or a way to make the kill certain, at the listed cost in time or work. A Novice beast that is not known is fought on its block.

### Adept — Enhancement, Dependency, Disruption

- **Enhancement.** One effect beyond any animal's range, stated as a rule and scaled as a technique of Adept tier would be (Personal or a small Circle). It is always on while the Dependency stands.
- **Dependency.** One thing on the ground the enhancement draws on: a den-site whose reading is off, a spring, a stand of trees, a carcass ground, a lick, a roost, a crust. The beast returns to it; the animal in it needs it. The Dependency is *found* by a reading of the layer the entry names, at Adept grade (Life: what the body needs; Structure: a shape or a reading where the map has none; Element: which element answers there; Boundary: a carcass ground's register), or by a record that already holds it. Finding the beast is not finding the Dependency.
- **Disruption.** What done at the Dependency ends the enhancement: a technique of a named school at Difficulty 16 at the site, or ordinary work over the stated time (a day's digging, a felled stand, a cut sandbar), or a legal act on Chimera ground that moves people off it. The entry lists both a practitioner route and a plain one where a plain one exists. Disruption is substrate work, not combat: a Disruption executed while the beast is present is executed under attack.
- **After.** The enhancement ends at once. The beast is the animal again, run on the Novice block with no trait unless the entry says it keeps one. It does not know that its enhancement has ended until it uses it.

### Master — Dominance, Reversal

- **Dominance.** On its ground and until its Reversal is executed, the beast has Favor on every check; its Guard is +2; the numbers rule (PM §7, three attackers) does not apply to it; and at the start of its turn it regains all lost Vigor, because the ground restores it. Its ground expresses the cell at strength wherever the beast is: the entry lists the effects (smoke, ambush, drowned ground, a fire line) as conditions on everyone in the Circle. A Master beast in Dominance cannot be killed by a party and is not meant to be; it can be driven off a scene (it withdraws at a quarter Vigor in a single turn, before regaining), and it can be held by a Guru edit for as long as the edit is paid.
- **Energy inversion.** The Dominance draws on the cell. When the cell turns — the phase changes, the fuel is gone, the water comes back — the draw reverses and the beast is at its weakest. The entry states the inversion as a condition and the Reversal as the operation that produces the condition on purpose.
- **Reversal.** A phase-scale operation, or a Ground-scale technique, that produces the inversion: a counter-burn across a hill, an oasis collapsed, a waterhole raised a mile away, a range held empty across two phase turns. Executing it is downtime work priced in labor-days, in contracts, or in a Guru's Marks, and it has a last act that is a scene. The Reversal is *identified* by a Master-grade reading of the layer the entry names at Difficulty 22, by a Join, or by a record: the Shalei hunters of 1156 had the oasis from three caravan ledgers, not from a reading.
- **After.** Dominance ends. The beast is run on the Master block without the Dominance line: killable, fighting, and by the canon payload fighting hardest now. It does not leave its ground. It dies there or the party does.

### Guru — Domain, Tether, Displacement

- **Domain.** A Ground (a valley, a lake basin, a forest reach, a harbor approach) that expresses the cell at full strength for as long as the embodiment stands. The entry lists the Domain's effects at Ground scale as standing conditions; the GMG's Environmental Strain rule (GMG §3) applies inside it: a Novice of the moon's own school takes 1 Strain at the start of each turn spent reading inside the Domain, as a Necrotic Novice does on a battlefield, and every reading of that layer inside the Domain returns one grade more in facts, at the reader's own scale (a Novice's one vague fact becomes two, one of them precise; the Circle and the Ground stay gated by rank), because the layer is louder than the reader. Lesser emergences inside a Domain may reach Master tier, whatever the homeland's ceiling says elsewhere; the Domain is the reading.
- **No block.** A Guru-tier emergence is not fought. If it presents a body — the parishes at Frostvatn said it did — that body is run as a Master block in Dominance, and when Downed it is gone until the next phase turn and then present again, because the tether was not touched. Killing the body is a record of a body killed and nothing else. This is the module's rule for "could not be killed" (register row 9).
- **Tether.** A location: the anchor by which the embodiment holds the Ground. The anchor is the two values a Structure reading at Guru grade returns as editable; it is what a keeper's closure holds empty; it is the headwater the Iselva diversion cut. It is never the beast's body.
- **Displacement.** Two methods exist in the record. *Engineering* (Accord, Frostvatn 1230–32): unseat the anchor by altering the terrain it is tethered to — divert a headwater, cut a seawall, dry a basin — across at least two phase turns, at the price the Frostvatn ledger names (three Gurus' Marks). *Closure* (Chimera, Marama 1091): a keeper's closure of the ground, held empty across two phase turns and renewed at each, after which the Watch records the reading fallen; the Watch does not know why it worked. Either method ends in a scene whose last act is a **Join at Difficulty 30** (GMG §4): two schools, each at 22, on their own layer of the anchor — Structure and Element for an engineering displacement; Life and Structure, or Life and Boundary, for a closure. The Domain collapses when the Join succeeds. Nothing else displaces a Guru tier; damage does not, and no single school does.

### Herds, packs, swarms, and colonies as Lines

Where the base animal comes in numbers — a swarm, a sounder, a herd, a colony's soldiers — the entry runs it as a Line (GMG §6) at Squad scale: Cohesion 6, Guard 12, attack d20 + 3, damage d10 + 1, with the entry's Move and its tier rule on top. A swarm has no officer; it breaks at 0 Cohesion into nothing worth counting. Techniques that name Cohesion work on it as on soldiers: *Volley*, *Sweep*, *Force at Scale*, a fire.

### Encounter calibration

By the platoon standard (GMG §6): a Novice beast is a fight for one Adept or two Novices; two or three Novice beasts, or a Squad-scale swarm, for a Novice party. An Adept beast is a fight for an Adept party, and a losing one until the Dependency is found. A Master beast in Dominance is beyond a party; after Reversal it engages a Master with a Squad, or a party of Adepts and one Master on equal terms. A Guru tier is a campaign event: a Displacement is a season of play, and its cost ledger is the arc.

### What an emergence leaves

A relic (PM §10; GMG §9). The tier's outcome line is where it comes from, and the reading is what makes it separable from the body:

- **Novice.** The Exploit executed, or the beast killed with its Rigidity known: the Trait's material. Killed on its block with nothing known: a carcass.
- **Adept.** The Disruption executed: material from the Dependency site, which is still there after the beast is an animal again. The animal's body carries nothing.
- **Master.** The beast killed after its Reversal: the Dominance's remains. Driven off, it leaves nothing.
- **Guru.** The Displacement Join succeeded: a fragment of the tether. A body Downed leaves a record of a body.

The relic's domain is the beast's own line — its trait, enhancement, or dominance, read into the PM §10 table by the GM — and its moon is the emergence's. Entries in section 3 carry no relic field; the GM writes the relic from the entry when the outcome line is reached.

### Records

Every count a beast entry carries names its counter (GMG §5). The parish counts what it tithes, the Ledger what it licenses, the Concord what a claimant reports, a caravan house what it lost. Two records of one beast disagree, and both are handed out as the scene puts them in reach. A beast's date is the date of the record, not of the emergence; the Watch's phase entry is a reading, not a sighting.

### Entry format

Each entry gives, in order: **designation** (ground, descriptor, phase and year of record) — tier · base animal · biome × moon: the cell · node reading (record) · ground's institution. Then *Ecology* (what the cell changed, range, season, sign); *Block*; the tier's rule lines; *Layers* (the layers that return something; unlisted layers return nothing here); *Records*. The designation is the XI.3 name field; nothing in it is a coined word.

## 3. The homelands

### 3.0 Ceilings and rolls of record

**Ceilings.** The Firstday Watch's phase ledger, Velquor 1245, one figure per homeland, with the ground that carries it and the record that disagrees. All twelve are [N] (register row 4). Frostvatn's basin is not read here: it is reserved to the episodes (Canon XI.5, item 17).

| Homeland | Ceiling (Watch, Velquor 1245) | Ground at the ceiling | Second record |
|:--|:-:|:--|:--|

| Grimskov | Adept | Ulvskov timber stands; the Svarthavet coast at Stenhavn reads Adept with tidal distortion above Velquor norms | The Stenhavn moot's tide log says the coast reads higher than the Watch's instrument |

### 3.1 Isavík — Menneske · Gold Crown · Tundra, Taiga, Evergreen

Ormsvík (harbor seat, evergreen coast), Hvítadal (tundra valley), Skarfell (taiga ridge). Ceiling Master in the northern valleys; Adept on the coast and the ridge. Ethos: Devout. The parishes file beasts on the tithe roll as stock lost; the moots count them in winters, as they count everything; the Skarfell fire-house keeps the hunters' tally, which is the one that is usually right. Any Isavík scene inherits the silence of 1230 (Canon Part VII, Frictions): a beast in the northern valleys is read by the parish as a beast and by the households as something that kept an appointment, and no one at the table should settle it.

**Hvítadal ring-ox, Namaris 1244** — Novice · musk ox (a bull and a ring of nine) · Tundra × Namaris: whiteout glare, false suns · node Master-active, the valley (Watch) · Devout ground.
*Ecology.* The herd wintered in the resettled valley under the Namaris glare and formed the ring at every approach for a phase without breaking it; the glare that blinds a sledge team does not reach the ox, whose eye is set for it. Sign: a ring of trodden snow that does not move, and a false sun standing over it at noon.
*Block.* Large: Guard 11 · Vigor 18 · attack +1 + d4 · horn d8 + 1 + Rank Die · Move 8. Ring of nine: run the ring as a Squad Line (Cohesion 6) around the bull. *Amplified trait:* the ring's stand — anything that enters the ring's Circle is charged by the bull with Favor, and the ring does not lose Cohesion to fear.
*Rigidity.* The ring forms at any approach and never leaves its ground to pursue. *Exploit:* walk around it; the valley's sledge road can be rerouted in a day's work along the far bank, and the parish's shrine ground is the only thing the ring is standing on.
*Layers.* Life (Novice): well, and afraid of the light. Element: the glare's next hour. Field — Nerve: the ring holds; the bull holds. Field — Geometry: where the ring will open, which is nowhere.
*Records.* The parish tithe roll counts the herd as the valley's stock, as it counts the valley whole (Canon Part V, Population Magnitudes). The moot counts nine and a bull and one winter.

**Ormsvík wound-seal, Saelura 1244** — Novice · grey seal, bull · Evergreen coast × Saelura: rapid healing · node Adept-active (Watch) · Devout ground.
*Ecology.* A bull that hauls out on one skerry below the harbor chapel and closes a harpoon wound within the turn. The sealers have taken it three times by their count and it has come back with the scars. Sign: a skerry with more seals on it than the tide should allow, and no gulls.
*Block.* Large, in water: Guard 12 (14 in water) · Vigor 20 · attack +1 + d4 · bite d8 + 1 + Rank Die · Move 4 on rock, 12 in water. *Amplified trait:* regains d4 Vigor at the start of each of its turns.
*Rigidity.* Hauls out on the same skerry at the same tide, every day the harbor is clear, and will not haul out elsewhere. *Exploit:* take the skerry at low water before it arrives; it will not haul out onto a crew and will not fight in the water for a rock. A kill needs it out of the water past the turn it regains in.
*Layers.* Life (Adept): the wound closes as you watch; what it needs is the skerry's weed-bed. Structure: mass, and a haul-out worn to a groove. Field — Nerve: it holds on the rock, breaks in the surf.
*Records.* The harbor-master's sealskin tally (three taken, none landed) and the parish's (none lost — a seal is not stock).

**Skarfell bog-lynx, Velquor 1244** — Novice · lynx · Taiga × Velquor: bog-light, drowned ground · node Adept-active, the ridge (Watch) · Devout ground.
*Ecology.* The Velquor bog-lights on the ridge's low ground came up along the drowned trails, and the lynx hunts along them; it has taken dogs from the fire-house's sledge teams four winters running. Sign: lights in a line at dusk, and a lynx's prints that never break the crust.
*Block.* Guard 13 · Vigor 12 · attack +1 + d4 · bite d6 + 1 + Rank Die · Move 10, unchanged on drowned ground. *Amplified trait:* never Stuck and never slowed on bog; a pursuer on drowned ground makes a Frame check at 13 each turn or is Stuck.
*Rigidity.* Hunts only along the line of the lights and turns back where they end. *Exploit:* the Skarfell hunters' habit — they walk the lit line before dusk and stake it, and the lynx does not cross a stake; the fire-house calls this wood-luck and the parish sacrist who lives in the same longhouse calls it nothing (Canon Part VII, Skoglind).
*Layers.* Element (Novice): the lights are the ground's, not a fire's; where the drowned ground is. Field — Ground: the one dry path, which is the lynx's. Boundary: dogs, recent, several, along the line.
*Records.* The fire-house tally: four dogs, four winters. The parish: no entry.

**Hvítadal false-sun roost, Namaris 1244** — Adept · raven (a roost of some sixty) · Tundra × Namaris: whiteout glare, false suns · node Master-active, the valley (Watch) · Devout ground.
*Ecology.* The roost holds a crag on the valley's east face that catches the false suns; under them the birds call together, and the calling and the glare take direction from anyone below. The resettled households lost two sledge teams to the wrong side of the valley in one phase. Sign: a crag that seems to have two suns behind it, and ravens that do not scatter at a shot.
*Block.* Run the roost as a Squad Line (Cohesion 6, Guard 14, attack d20 + 3, damage d10 + 1, Move 12, flying). *Enhancement:* within a Circle of 20 paces under the roost's calling, Notice fails (Difficulty +6) and any character crossing the ground moves the direction the GM names rather than the one the player does, unless a Field — Ground reading is held; mounts and dogs bolt on a Reserve check at 13.
*Dependency.* The crag face: its reading is off, and the roost's calling is the crag's glare thrown back as sound. Found by Structure at Adept grade (the face returns a composition that is not stone where the glare strikes) or by Element (the light answers here and nowhere else in the valley).
*Disruption.* Arcane *Precise Force* or Elemental *Shape* (ground) at the ledges, Difficulty 16, three successes across a scene; or the households' plain route — cut the ledges with picks from above, two days' work, under the roost. The parish's route is a Namaris rite on the crag, which the sacrist has offered and the households have declined.
*After.* Ravens. They stay, and they still call.
*Layers.* Structure (Adept): the face is not stone at the strike-line; precise mass of the ledge. Element (Adept): light answers at the crag. Intent: fear on the households, and something else the Divine reader cannot name and the rules do not narrate. Field — Ground: the safe path, at Hindrance under the calling.
*Records.* The parish roll: two teams lost to weather. The households' count: two teams, and where.

**Ormsvík sap-bear, Saelura 1244** — Adept · brown bear, sow · Evergreen coast × Saelura: rapid healing · node Adept-active (Watch) · Devout ground.
*Ecology.* A sow denning above the harbor's timber landing in a stand where the sap rose in Saelura out of season; she feeds on it and her wounds close. She has killed one sealer and turned a Paladin escort of four back to the chapel. Sign: a stand of evergreens weeping sap in the wrong phase, bark stripped to head height.
*Block.* Large: Guard 13 · Vigor 24 · attack +2 + d6 · claw d10 + 2 + Rank Die · Move 8. *Enhancement:* regains Rank Die Vigor at the start of each of her turns while within 100 paces of the stand; ignores the first level of Exhausted and the first Frightened effect each scene.
*Dependency.* The stand — the sap. Found by Life at Adept grade by contact with a stripped tree (what the body needs: this) or by Element (water answers in the wood, and should not).
*Disruption.* Tap the stand dry: a day's work with augers and buckets by the timber landing's crew, or Elemental *Still* (water) at Difficulty 16 held across the stand for three turns, or fell it — which the harbor factor would sell and the parish has not forbidden.
*After.* A bear, and a sow with cubs in the spring, which is worse for the landing and a different problem.
*Layers.* Life (Adept): the wound closes; needs the stand. Element (Adept): water answers in the trees. Boundary: one man, this phase, violent. Field — Nerve: she holds; she does not break for fire.
*Records.* The parish tithe roll: one sealer, one column turned, filed as weather and a bear. The harbor factor's tally: eleven trees stripped and the price of each.

### 3.2 Grimskov — Menneske · Blue Accord · Tundra, Taiga, Grassland

Ulvskov (taiga timber town), Stenhavn (stone harbor, tundra coast), Kaldmark (grassland garrison). Ceiling Adept. Ethos: Rationalist. Beasts are cull licences — the Ledger's examiners issue them by school and invoice whichever house the beast cost, and a cull is an entry in the homeland budget below the Escrow lease and above nothing. The moot hears each licence and the examiners note that the hearing serves no procedural function. The Kaldmark garrison's remount officer keeps the count on the grassland; the timber houses keep it at Ulvskov; the harbor-master keeps the tide log and everything the tide brings.

**Stenhavn aurora-fox, Orrivane 1244** — Novice · arctic fox · Tundra coast × Orrivane: aurora hallucination · node Adept-active (Watch) · Rationalist ground.
*Ecology.* A dog fox on the fish-drying racks above the harbor whose winter coat throws back the aurora; under it, a watcher sees two foxes, then none. It has cleared racks worth a household's phase. Sign: racks stripped from the top, and the watchman's report that he shot at the second fox.
*Block.* Small: Guard 15 · Vigor 6 · attack +1 + d4 · bite d4 + 1 + Rank Die · Move 12. *Amplified trait:* under the aurora, attacks against it have Hindrance and it cannot be targeted at all beyond 10 paces.
*Rigidity.* Raids the same racks on the third night after each clear night, from the seaward end. *Exploit:* the racks; the harbor-master's watch stands at the seaward end on the third night and the fox comes to the spear. A kill is one shot at Favor within 10 paces.
*Layers.* Structure (Novice): one small mass, moving, where two are seen. Field — Ground: the approach along the shingle. Life: well, and hungry.
*Records.* The harbor-master's rack tally, in fish. The Ledger's cull licence, in eighths, for a Novice of any school.

**Ulvskov timber-sounder, Threnis 1244** — Novice · wild boar (a sow and a sounder of eleven) · Taiga × Threnis: pack coordination · node Adept-active (Watch) · Rationalist ground.
*Ecology.* The sounder took the skid-roads below the Ulvskov stands in Threnis and runs them as one animal; it has broken two log-sledges and a teamster's leg. Sign: skid-road banks rooted flat for a hundred paces, and eleven sets of prints in a single line.
*Block.* Run as a Squad Line (Cohesion 6, Guard 12, attack d20 + 3, damage d10 + 1, Move 10); the sow separately: Guard 12 · Vigor 16 · attack +1 + d4 · tusk d8 + 1 + Rank Die. *Amplified trait:* the sounder acts on the sow's initiative and charges as one; its charge on a road throws anyone in the road Prone on a Frame check at 13.
*Rigidity.* The sounder follows the sow and nothing else. *Exploit:* the sow. Kill her, drive her, or *Quiet* her (Nature Adept), and the sounder is eleven boars scattering into the stands; the timber house's contract pays on the sow alone.
*Layers.* Field — Geometry (Novice): the skid-road is the corridor; the sounder comes through it and nowhere else. Field — Weight: the sow commits; the rest follow. Life: the sow is old and lame in the off fore.
*Records.* The timber house's tally of ruined road, in days of re-laying. The Ledger's licence, issued to a Warden of Adept rank at 3 seals.

**Kaldmark recovery-band, Saelura 1244** — Novice · horse (a stallion and a band of seven mares) · Grassland × Saelura: soil recovery · node Adept-active (Watch) · Rationalist ground.
*Ecology.* A feral band on the regrown ground south of the garrison, where the Saelura soil came back thick; the stallion runs a day without blowing. The remount officer wants the band and has lost two riders' horses trying. Sign: grass grazed in a straight edge, and a stallion that does not tire.
*Block.* Large: Guard 12 · Vigor 20 · attack +1 + d4 · hoof d8 + 1 + Rank Die · Move 14. *Amplified trait:* never Exhausted; a rider pursuing it on any other horse makes a Reserve check at 13 for the mount each turn after the third or the mount stops.
*Rigidity.* The band will not leave the recovered ground; driven to its edge, it turns along it. *Exploit:* fence the edge. The garrison can run a rope line across the narrow end in a day, and the band turns into the corner it always turns into; the officer's count says the band has done this twice and been let out twice by riders who did not know.
*Layers.* Life (Novice): well; the stallion more than well. Field — Ground: the edge of the recovered ground, which is the band's whole map. Element (Adept): ground answers; the soil is the thing that changed.
*Records.* The remount officer's count: eight head, two lost. The Ledger's assessment: horses are Kaldmark's export and a feral band is unregistered stock, licence 1 seal.

**Ulvskov smoke-bear, Namaris 1244** — Adept · black bear, boar · Taiga × Namaris: crown fire · node Adept-active (Watch) · Rationalist ground.
*Ecology.* A crown fire ran the ridge stands in Namaris and did not go out; it holds in the tops of a line of dead pines and the bear hunts under it, in the smoke, taking sledge dogs and one timber-cutter. Sign: a fire line in the treetops that the rain does not end, and a bear's prints in the ash.
*Block.* Large: Guard 13 · Vigor 24 · attack +2 + d6 · claw d10 + 2 + Rank Die · Move 8. *Enhancement:* immune to Burning; in smoke (the fire line's Circle, 20 paces) it is concealed, its attacks have Favor, and anyone else there is Sickened on a Reserve check at 13 each turn.
*Dependency.* The fire line: it hunts in the smoke and eats what the smoke drops. Found by Element at Adept grade (fire answers in the crowns and will do so next turn, and the turn after) or by a Ledger fire-warden's map, which exists.
*Disruption.* Put the line out. Elemental *Still* (fire) at Difficulty 16, held three turns across the line's Circle, ends it; or the timber house cuts a break below the line, four days with a crew of twenty, the price of which is in its complaint to the examiners.
*After.* A black bear in a burned stand with nothing to eat, which leaves.
*Layers.* Element (Adept): fire answers in the crowns; next turn it holds. Life (Adept, contact): the bear's lungs are clear, which they should not be; what it needs is the smoke. Boundary: one cutter, this phase, confused. Field — Nerve: it holds in the smoke and breaks in the open.
*Records.* The timber house's contract: one cutter's household paid, four days of a crew. The Ledger's licence: Elemental Adept, fire, 5 seals, Namaris price.

**Stenhavn bluff-herd, Threnis 1244** — Adept · reindeer (a herd of some forty, one lead bull) · Tundra coast × Threnis: herd-beast emergence · node Adept-active (Watch) · Rationalist ground.
*Ecology.* The herd came down the coast bluffs above the harbor in Threnis and runs the shingle at every tide-turn; the run has taken the harbor road twice and a cart with it. Sign: a herd that runs the same line at every turn of the tide, and lichen grazed off the bluff face to a hard line.
*Block.* Run as a Squad Line (Cohesion 6, Guard 12, attack d20 + 3, damage d10 + 1, Move 12); the bull: Guard 12 · Vigor 20 · attack +2 + d6 · antler d8 + 2 + Rank Die. *Enhancement:* the herd's run — everything in the run's path (a corridor 5 paces wide along its line) is Prone on a Frame check at 16 and takes d8; the herd does not lose Cohesion to damage from anything it runs over.
*Dependency.* A mineral lick on the bluff face, under the lichen line, where the bull leads at every turn. Found by Life at Adept grade by contact with the bull or a carcass (what it needs: salt, from there) or by Structure (the lick's composition is not the bluff's).
*Disruption.* Bury the lick: Elemental *Shape* (ground) at Difficulty 16, two casts; or the harbor's crew brings the face down with bars at low tide, a day, under the run. The moot has proposed salting the harbor road instead, which the examiners have filed as serving no procedural function and which would work.
*After.* Reindeer, forty of them, which the harbor eats.
*Layers.* Structure (Adept): the lick is not bluff. Life (Adept): salt, from the face. Field — Geometry: the corridor, exact. Element: ground is stable; the tide is not (tidal distortion above Velquor norms is in the log).
*Records.* The harbor-master's tide log, which now carries the herd beside the depth. The Ledger's licence: Warden, Adept, 4 seals; the moot's hearing, noted.

**Kaldmark spring-pack, Orrivane 1244** — Adept · wolf (a pack of six) · Grassland × Orrivane: herd agitation · node Adept-active (Watch) · Rationalist ground.
*Ecology.* The pack drinks at a spring on the remount pasture that came up in Orrivane, and every herd that drinks after it bolts; the pack takes what the bolting breaks. The garrison's horse lines have stampeded twice. Sign: a spring with no herd within a mile of it and wolf-sign all round it.
*Block.* Six wolves on one initiative: Guard 13 · Vigor 12 · attack +2 + d6 · bite d8 + 2 + Rank Die · Move 12 each. *Enhancement:* any herd, mount, or Line within 30 paces of a pack member makes a Cohesion or Reserve check at 13 at the start of its turn or scatters and bolts; the pack has Favor against anything bolting.
*Dependency.* The spring. Found by Element at Adept grade (water answers here; the water is the agitation) or by Life (the pack needs the spring, not the herds).
*Disruption.* Elemental *Still* (water) at Difficulty 16, three turns, or *Shape* (ground) to fill it, two casts; or the garrison fills it with a wagon of stone in half a day, which the remount officer has requisitioned twice and been refused twice as unbudgeted.
*After.* Wolves on a grassland with a garrison on it, which lasts a phase.
*Layers.* Element (Adept): water answers; it will answer next turn. Life (Adept): the pack is well; what it needs is the spring. Field — Weight: which wolf commits, and to what. Intent: nothing here; the garrison's fear, at the lines.
*Records.* The remount officer's count: two stampedes, nine horses. The Ledger's licence: Elemental Adept, water, 5 seals, Orrivane price — cheap, and still refused.

### 3.3 Zhenshui — Renlei · Blue Accord · Taiga, Evergreen, Grassland

Baishui (river seat; the First Examiner's seat), Songlin (evergreen pine town), Yunmen (highland gate, grassland trade). Ceiling Adept. Ethos: Rationalist, in the seat of the registry itself. A beast at Baishui is a licence before it is anything, and the licence is a board matter: certified hunters, a phase-priced fee, a return filed with the count of kills. Three certified returns on one beast disagree as a matter of course, and the examiner of higher standing who resolves them may be a season away. Renlei wait.

**Baishui towpath-dholes, Threnis 1243** — Novice · dhole (a pack of eight) · Taiga × Threnis: pack coordination · node Adept-active, the reaches (Watch) · Rationalist ground.
*Ecology.* The pack hunts the Lianshui towpaths above the seat at dusk, running the barge-ox teams into the canal; it has drowned two oxen and a bargeman. Sign: a tow-team that will not walk the bank after the lanterns are lit.
*Block.* Run as a Squad Line (Cohesion 6, Guard 12, attack d20 + 3, damage d10 + 1, Move 12). *Amplified trait:* the pack moves as one; it never loses Cohesion for a member killed, only for a member that flees, and none does.
*Rigidity.* Hunts the towpath at dusk, from the upstream end, and only when a team is on it. *Exploit:* a lit team on the towpath at dusk with a certified Warden at the upstream end; the pack comes down the path in a line and *Volley* takes its Cohesion. The barge-masters' plain route is to lie up at dusk, which costs a day a phase and which they do.
*Layers.* Field — Geometry (Novice): the towpath is the corridor. Field — Weight: the pack commits when the team is mid-bank. Boundary: one man, this year, water.
*Records.* The barge-masters' log: two oxen, one man. The Ledger's licence: Warden, Novice or higher, 2 seals; the return says eight killed, and the pack is still there, which the examiner has queried.

**Songlin ridge-leopard, Threnis 1244** — Novice · leopard · Evergreen × Threnis: apex beast emergence · node Adept-active (Watch) · Rationalist ground.
*Ecology.* A leopard in the pine stands above the town that has taken goats, a dog, and a woodcutter's child, and has been shot at nine times by the board's count without a hit. Sign: kills hung in one pine at the ridge top, and no bird in that tree.
*Block.* Guard 14 · Vigor 14 · attack +1 + d4 · bite d8 + 1 + Rank Die · Move 10, climbs at full Move. *Amplified trait:* in pine shade it cannot be targeted beyond 5 paces and it is never Surprised.
*Rigidity.* Every kill goes to the same tree and it returns to feed on the second night. *Exploit:* the tree, on the second night, with the bow already drawn (a Warden on *Watch* is not Surprised and shoots first).
*Layers.* Field — Ground (Novice): the approach to the tree, one, from below. Life: well; a wound in the flank, old. Boundary (Adept): a child, this phase, violent, and the tree's register is a feeding-ground.
*Records.* The Songlin board's return: nine shots, none landed, three hunters' fees. The town's count: one child, and the fee is not the point.

**Yunmen fire-runners, Namaris 1244** — Novice · wild ass (a herd of thirty) · Grassland × Namaris: wildfire front · node Adept-active (Watch) · Rationalist ground.
*Ecology.* A herd that runs ahead of the grass fires on the highland and has come down the gate road into the caravan yards twice. Sign: smoke on the highland and dust on the road ahead of it.
*Block.* Run as a Squad Line (Cohesion 6, Guard 12, attack d20 + 3, damage d10 + 1, Move 14). *Amplified trait:* Move 14, and its run gives Prone on a Frame check at 13 to anything in its path.
*Rigidity.* Runs downslope toward the gate road every time, from the same saddle. *Exploit:* the road. The gate's toll-keeper can close the yard gates and open the drove-way south in a quarter hour, and the herd runs through and past; the caravan houses' complaint is that it runs through their strings.
*Layers.* Element (Novice): fire on the highland, upwind. Field — Geometry: the saddle is the corridor. Field — Ground: how far the smoke is.
*Records.* The toll-keeper's count of overturned carts, by phase. The Ledger's licence, not issued: the herd is unregistered stock and the yards are a guild-house lease.

**Songlin tiger, Threnis 1244** — Adept · tiger · Evergreen × Threnis: apex beast emergence · node Adept-active (Watch) · Rationalist ground.
*Ecology.* A tiger in the deep pine north of the town that drinks at one spring before every hunt and has killed four of the board's certified hunters in a phase. Sign: a spring with a worn path to it from every direction but one, and silence in the pines an hour before dusk.
*Block.* Large: Guard 14 · Vigor 26 · attack +2 + d6 · bite d10 + 2 + Rank Die · Move 12. *Enhancement:* its roar — everyone within 20 paces is Frightened on a Reserve check at 13; and while the spring stands, it regains Rank Die Vigor at the start of each turn spent within the pines.
*Dependency.* The spring, which reads Threnis-active in the pine root. Found by Life at Adept grade by contact with a kill or a track (what it needs: the spring, before the hunt) or by Element (water answers in the roots).
*Disruption.* Elemental *Shape* (ground) at Difficulty 16, three casts, to turn the spring under the roots; or dig it out and channel it downslope, two days with picks, under the pines. The board licensed the digging at Threnis price and no crew took it.
*After.* A tiger, which is still a tiger; run on the Novice block with the roar kept as its trait.
*Layers.* Life (Adept): the spring, before the hunt. Element (Adept): water answers in the roots and will not stop. Boundary (Master): four crossings, this phase, each a hunter who saw the tiger from the front. Field — Nerve: it holds; it does not break for numbers.
*Records.* The Songlin board's return: four hunters' families paid from the licence fund; the town's count: four, and the price of tiger bone, which the board does not record.

**Baishui drift-herons, Orrivane 1244** — Adept · grey heron (a colony of twenty) · Taiga river × Orrivane: compass drift · node Adept-active (Watch) · Rationalist ground.
*Ecology.* The colony nests a sandbar the Lianshui laid down in Orrivane below the seat; under the colony, barges lose the channel and ground on a bar the charts do not show, and three have. Sign: a sandbar that was not there in Namaris, herons standing on it in a ring, and a barge-master swearing at his compass.
*Block.* Run as a Squad Line (Cohesion 6, Guard 14, attack d20 + 3, damage d10 + 1, Move 10, flying). *Enhancement:* within 30 paces of the bar, bearings fail — any Notice to hold a course is at Difficulty 19; a Structure reading at Adept grade returns the true position with the note that it moved a pace since the reading began; boats circle unless a reading is held each turn.
*Dependency.* The bar itself: its substrate reading drifts, and the colony nests on the drift. Found by Structure at Adept grade (a mass whose position is not where the Overlay puts it) or by the portal station's schedule, which has recorded the delays without knowing why.
*Disruption.* Cut the bar: Elemental *Work at Scale* (water, harbor sub-discipline) held three turns, Master work; or Elemental *Shape* (water) at Difficulty 16, six casts across two days; or the barge-masters' plain route, a train of empty barges dragged across it at high water for a day, which the canal board has scheduled for the Saelura turn.
*After.* Herons on a bar, which the river takes by Threnis.
*Layers.* Structure (Adept): the bar moved a pace; its composition is river silt and something the Overlay files as anecdotal. Field — Ground: the channel is where the birds are not. Life: twenty herons, well, nesting out of season.
*Records.* The canal board's grounding log: three barges, one cargo lost. The portal station's schedule: eleven late departures in Orrivane, attributed to the river.

### 3.4 Tienling — Renlei · Blue Accord · Evergreen, Grassland, Desert

Shihmen (evergreen foothill gate), Pingyeh (grassland market), Shakou (desert-edge caravan post), Shakoui (evergreen-coast harbor). Ceiling Master, in the Shalei; Adept elsewhere. Ethos: Rationalist, administered by guild houses. The caravan houses keep the desert's record as a road-closure tally and a stragglers' ledger; the Shakou road has been closed by a beast once in the calendar (1155) and the houses price every phase against it. No Master rolled here; the Shalei's precedent stands in XI.3 and the ceiling is the reason the houses post a rear guard.

**Shakou mirage-jackal, Velquor 1244** — Novice · golden jackal · Desert × Velquor: mirages · node Master-active, the Shalei (Watch) · Rationalist ground.
*Ecology.* Shadows the strings at the road's mirage-line at dusk and takes stragglers — a lame camel, a walker. Sign: a jackal that is on the horizon and then not, and a straggler's pack found intact.
*Block.* Small: Guard 15 · Vigor 8 · attack +1 + d4 · bite d4 + 1 + Rank Die · Move 12. *Amplified trait:* in Velquor, beyond 10 paces it cannot be targeted; within, attackers have Hindrance.
*Rigidity.* Holds the mirage-line, a fixed distance behind the last animal, and closes only on one that falls more than that behind. *Exploit:* the rear guard; a string that keeps its last animal inside the line is never touched, which is the houses' standing order and is obeyed until the third phase out.
*Layers.* Field — Ground (Novice): the distance, exact, which the eye cannot give. Life: hungry, thin. Boundary: walkers, several, over years, empty.
*Records.* Three caravan houses' stragglers' ledgers, which do not agree on the count and agree on the line.

**Shihmen gate-boar, Saelura 1244** — Novice · wild boar, boar · Evergreen foothill × Saelura: rapid healing · node Adept-active (Watch) · Rationalist ground.
*Ecology.* Roots the terraces of the gate road every night and has been speared twice by the gate watch; both wounds closed by morning. Sign: a terrace wall thrown down in a straight line, nightly.
*Block.* Large: Guard 12 · Vigor 20 · attack +1 + d4 · tusk d8 + 1 + Rank Die · Move 10. *Amplified trait:* regains d4 Vigor at the start of each turn.
*Rigidity.* The same terrace, the second below the gate, from the downhill end, before midnight. *Exploit:* the terrace; a pit on the downhill end, dug in a day, takes it out of the turn it regains in.
*Layers.* Life (Novice): well; the wound is not there. Field — Seams: where the wall breaks, which is where it enters. Field — Ground: the downhill approach.
*Records.* The gate's toll ledger: two terraces a phase, in labor-days owed by the farmers who hold them.

**Pingyeh ring-voles, Velquor 1244** — Novice · burrowing vole (a colony) · Grassland × Velquor: ring necrosis · node Adept-active (Watch) · Rationalist ground.
*Ecology.* Rings of dead wheat spreading from the colony's burrows across the dryland fields; each ring widens a pace a night. Sign: circles in the standing wheat, dead to the root, in Velquor.
*Block.* A colony, not a fight: run its soldiers, if dug into, as a Squad Line (Cohesion 6, Guard 12, attack d20 + 3, damage d4, Move 4). *Amplified trait:* the ring — nothing grows inside it and nothing recovers Vigor at rest inside it.
*Rigidity.* The ring widens at one pace a night from a burrow at its exact center, and the colony never starts a second ring while the first stands. *Exploit:* the center. Dig it at the first ring (a morning's work) and the ring stops; find it by pacing the ring's radius, which any farmer can do and the market's grain factors pay them not to do until the harvest is assessed.
*Layers.* Life (Novice): dying, in a circle. Boundary (Novice): nothing died here — the ring is not a crossing. Structure (Adept): the burrow at the center, precise.
*Records.* The Pingyeh market's assessment of lost wheat, by field. The farmers' count, in rings.

**Shakoui tide-crabs, Velquor 1244** — Novice · shore crab (a swarm) · Coastal × Velquor: tidal distortion · node Adept-active (Watch) · Rationalist ground.
*Ecology.* The distorted tide brings the swarm up over the quays at the wrong hour and it strips whatever is landed: fish, hides, a sleeping deckhand's fingers. Sign: a tide that comes when the Ledger's table says it should not, and the quay moving.
*Block.* Run as a Squad Line (Cohesion 6, Guard 12, attack d20 + 3, damage d10 + 1, Move 6). *Amplified trait:* the swarm's bite leaves Stuck (Difficulty 10) for a turn on anyone it damages.
*Rigidity.* Comes up on the wrong tide exactly, to the same quay, and goes down with it. *Exploit:* the tide. The harbor keeps the Ledger's tide table; the customs cutters' officers keep a second, corrected by hand since 1218, and the swarm follows the second. A crew that lands by the officers' table is never on the quay when it comes.
*Layers.* Element (Novice): water answers at the wrong hour. Structure (Adept): the swarm's mass, and the tide's, precise. Field — Ground: the quay's one dry corner.
*Records.* The Ledger's tide table, wrong. The officers' corrected copy, unfiled.

**Shakou oasis-camel, Saelura 1244** — Novice · dromedary, bull · Desert × Saelura: oasis stabilization · node Master-active, the Shalei (Watch) · Rationalist ground.
*Ecology.* A feral bull at the oasis a day south of the post, where the Saelura water held, that has held the water against three strings. Sign: an oasis with a camel at it and no string watering.
*Block.* Large: Guard 11 · Vigor 20 · attack +1 + d4 · bite and kick d8 + 1 + Rank Die · Move 10. *Amplified trait:* Frame — its bite and its kick each throw the target Rank Die paces and Prone.
*Rigidity.* Guards the water; will not leave it and will not drink elsewhere. *Exploit:* water elsewhere; Elemental *Draw Water* poured on the sand a hundred paces off draws it, and the strings water while it drinks. The houses' plain route is to water at night in relays, which is what they do.
*Layers.* Element (Novice): water answers here; stable. Life: well, and not in rut, which the drovers doubt. Field — Nerve: holds.
*Records.* The caravan houses' watering ledger: three strings turned, in days.

**Shakou storm-vultures, Namaris 1244** — Adept · griffon vulture (a colony of thirty) · Desert × Namaris: sandstorms · node Master-active, the Shalei (Watch) · Rationalist ground.
*Ecology.* The colony flies inside the Namaris storms along the road's storm-line and feeds on what the storms kill; its wake carries the storm's grit, and a string it circles cannot see the road. Sign: vultures where the sky is brown, and none where it is clear.
*Block.* Run as a Squad Line (Cohesion 6, Guard 14, attack d20 + 3, damage d10 + 1, Move 14, flying). *Enhancement:* within 30 paces of the colony, concealment for it and against everyone; ranged attacks and Notice have Hindrance; unprotected eyes take 1 damage a turn.
*Dependency.* The carcass ground at the road's storm-line, a mile of drift where every phase's dead stock lies. Found by Boundary at Adept grade (many crossings, empty, in one place, across seasons) or by any house's stragglers' ledger.
*Disruption.* Move the road: the houses can shift the string-line a mile north of the drift across a phase, which strands the ground and the colony with it; or burn the ground — Elemental *Kindle* does not reach it, *Work at Scale* (fire) does, Master work, one turn held per hundred paces. Substrate work at the drift itself (Arcane *Precise Force* on the drift face, Difficulty 16, three successes) collapses the line the storm follows.
*After.* Vultures, which follow the strings as vultures do.
*Layers.* Boundary (Adept): stock, many, empty, here. Element (Adept): air answers; the storm turns along the drift. Field — Ground: the road's line, under grit, at Hindrance. Life (Novice): thirty, well, fed.
*Records.* The houses' stragglers' ledgers, three, disagreeing on the dead stock and agreeing on the mile.

**Shihmen agitator-troop, Orrivane 1244** — Adept · macaque (a troop of forty) · Evergreen foothill × Orrivane: herd agitation · node Adept-active (Watch) · Rationalist ground.
*Ecology.* A troop that roosts an outcrop grove above the gate road and whose calling sends oxen and camel strings off the road; six carts overturned in Orrivane. Sign: a grove on stone, macaques in it in silence, and then not.
*Block.* Run as a Squad Line (Cohesion 6, Guard 13, attack d20 + 3, damage d8, Move 10, climbing). *Enhancement:* draft animals and mounts within 30 paces of the troop's calling bolt on a Reserve check at 13 at the start of each turn; a bolting team's cart deals d10 to anyone in its road.
*Dependency.* The outcrop: the grove stands on stone that reads Orrivane-active, and the troop calls from it and nowhere else. Found by Structure at Adept grade (composition of the outcrop, precise, and a reading that is not stone's) or by the gate's map of overturnings, which all lie under the grove.
*Disruption.* Arcane *Precise Force* at the outcrop's fault, Difficulty 16, three successes; or fell the grove, which the gate's timber tax makes worth a day's crew and which the troop will contest.
*After.* Macaques in a felled grove, which raid the gate's stores for a phase and are then a different licence.
*Layers.* Structure (Adept): the outcrop's reading, off; precise mass. Field — Geometry: the road's one hinge, under the grove. Field — Weight: which macaque commits, which is none; the calling is not a commitment.
*Records.* The gate's toll ledger: six carts, cargo by manifest. The Ledger's licence: Sorcerer, Adept, 5 seals; the gate's petition says a Hexblade would be cheaper and the Ledger's reply says a Hexblade reads nothing.

### 3.5 Zulwazi — Umutu · Green Chimera · Savanna, Desert, Chaparral

Mbezwa (savanna market seat), Kwazira (chaparral highland town), Ulundwe (desert margin). Ceiling Master, on the Kwazira highland and the Mwamba foothills. Ethos: Reverie. Nothing is licensed. A beast is a hunting claim, a docket item at the Threnis sitting, a closure by a keeper lineage, and a range shift that moves a claim across a drove-line; the Concord records the claim and not the beast. The Ledger's Tinwara market returns are the only count from outside, and they count hides.

**Mbezwa reversed herd, Orrivane 1244** — Novice · wildebeest (a herd of some two hundred) · Savanna × Orrivane: migration reversal · node Adept-active (Watch) · Reverie ground.
*Ecology.* The herd came up the drove-lines against the cattle circuits in Orrivane and has held to them, running against every drive it meets. Sign: cattle backed up on a drove-line and dust coming toward them.
*Block.* Run as a Column Line (Cohesion 20, Guard 12, attack d20 + 10, damage d10 + 5, Move 12). *Amplified trait:* the run reverses whatever it meets; a herd or Line it strikes makes a Cohesion check at 16 or turns and runs with it.
*Rigidity.* Keeps to the drove-line, exactly, and does not leave it for grass. *Exploit:* a gap. The drovers open a line-gap at the Mbezwa fork with thorn-fence in a morning, and the herd takes the gap and runs into the dry; passage law says the herd does not stop, and this one does not.
*Layers.* Field — Geometry (Novice): the drove-line is the corridor. Life: well, and going the wrong way. Field — Nerve (Adept): the herd will not break; it will turn.
*Records.* The Mbezwa drovers' count: two hundred and the cattle days lost. The Tinwara market returns: hides down by a third, cause not recorded.

**Kwazira scrub-leopard, Threnis 1244** — Novice · leopard · Chaparral × Threnis: ambush predator magnification · node Master-active, the highland (Watch) · Reverie ground.
*Ecology.* Hunts the cattle path below the town from the downhill scrub at dawn and has taken a calf a phase and a herd-boy's arm. Sign: scrub trodden into a lie below the path, and the cattle bunching at one bend.
*Block.* Guard 14 · Vigor 14 · attack +1 + d4 · bite d8 + 1 + Rank Die · Move 10. *Amplified trait:* from concealment its first attack has Favor and deals +Rank Die; everyone in its Circle is Surprised in the first round unless on *Watch*.
*Rigidity.* Dawn, the downhill scrub, the one bend, the last animal. *Exploit:* drive at noon, or burn the scrub strip below the bend — a Kwazira lineage's burn, which the Zulwazi herders would protest at the Concord if it were anyone else's and do not when it is their own.
*Layers.* Field — Ground (Novice): the lie, from the path, at 4 paces. Field — Nerve: holds until the calf is down, then breaks. Life: well.
*Records.* The herd-boy's lineage: a calf a phase, an arm. The Concord: no item; a leopard is not a claim.

**Ulundwe salt-badger, Threnis 1244** — Novice · honey badger · Desert margin × Threnis: burrow dominance · node Adept-active (Watch) · Reverie ground.
*Ecology.* Digs under the salt-pan works at night toward the brine channels and collapses a pan a week; it has been speared and does not care. Sign: a pan gone to slurry overnight and a tunnel under its rim.
*Block.* Small: Guard 15 · Vigor 10 · attack +1 + d4 · bite d6 + 1 + Rank Die · Move 8, burrows 4. *Amplified trait:* ignores the first 3 damage of any hit; never Frightened; Stuck is a Difficulty 10 check for it.
*Rigidity.* Digs toward brine, nightly, the nearest channel first. *Exploit:* a decoy channel; the salt-cutters flood a dead pan at the works' edge and it digs there, a night's work to lay and a phase's peace. A kill needs it in the tunnel, where a spear reaches and it cannot turn.
*Layers.* Element (Novice): water answers, brine, underfoot. Field — Seams: where the pan's rim gives, which is where it is. Life: well, and annoyed.
*Records.* The salt-cutters' count of pans, in the salt they did not sell at Tinwara.

**Mbezwa dominance-pride, Threnis 1244** — Adept · lion (a pride of nine, one male) · Savanna × Threnis: pride dominance · node Adept-active (Watch) · Reverie ground.
*Ecology.* A pride holding a waterhole that stayed through the dry season on the Mbezwa side of a drove-line; the pride takes cattle at the water and the cattle will not be driven past it. Sign: a full waterhole in the dry, cattle bones round it, and one lion standing where the road was.
*Block.* Male: Guard 14 · Vigor 24 · attack +2 + d6 · bite d10 + 2 + Rank Die · Move 12. Eight lionesses on one initiative: Guard 13 · Vigor 16 · attack +2 + d6 · bite d8 + 2 + Rank Die · Move 12. *Enhancement:* while the male stands, the roar Frightens everyone within 30 paces (Reserve 13) and every lioness regains Rank Die Vigor at the start of her turn within sight of the water.
*Dependency.* The waterhole — the pride's dominance is the water's, held past its season. Found by Element at Adept grade (water answers here and the table is high) or by Life (what the pride needs: the water, not the cattle).
*Disruption.* Raise a second water a mile off: Elemental *Work at Scale* (water, well sub-discipline), Master work, a Circle's draw held three turns; or the drovers' plain route under water law — a well dug as give-back labor by the lineage whose claim the pride's range crossed, a phase's work counted in days, which splits the pride between two waters and ends the hold. The Concord has docketed the claim and deferred the well to the next Threnis turn, as it defers everything.
*After.* Lions at a waterhole, which the drovers drive past with losses they count.
*Layers.* Element (Adept): water answers; the table holds. Life (Adept): the water, not the cattle. Field — Weight: the male commits to the loudest thing. Intent: fear on the drovers, and a claimant's resolve, which the Divine reader files as nothing about the pride.
*Records.* The Concord docket, Threnis 1244: a hunting claim moved across a drove-line by the pride's range; objection by the drove-line's lineage; deferred. The Tinwara returns: nothing.

**Kwazira scrub-python, Threnis 1243** — Master · rock python · Chaparral (Mountain overlay) × Threnis: ambush predator magnification; predator magnification · node Master-active, the highland (Watch) · Reverie ground.
*Ecology.* A python of a size the highland has no record of, in the scrub above the town, that has made the whole highland its ambush ground. Since Threnis 1243 nothing on the highland is seen before it strikes; the Kwazira lineage closed the ground in Saelura 1244 and the closure has been renewed twice. It takes goats, dogs, and people at the rate of one a phase and has not been seen in the open. Sign: a highland with no birdsong, scrub that lies flat in a line a hand wide and thirty paces long, and cattle that will not go up.
*Block.* Large: Guard 15 (17 in Dominance) · Vigor 32 · attack +3 + d8 · bite d10 + 3 + Rank Die, then constriction: the target is Stuck (Difficulty 19) and takes d10 + 3 at the start of each of its turns held · Move 8. *Dominance:* on the highland, every creature is Surprised in the first round of any engagement (*Watch* excepted); the python's first attack each engagement has Favor and is from concealment; it regains all Vigor at the start of its turn; the numbers rule does not apply to it; Guard +2. The ground expresses the cell: the scrub is cover for it and for nothing else — anyone else in it is at Hindrance to Notice and has no cover against the python.
*Energy inversion.* Its dominance is the scrub's cover, magnified. Burn the cover and the highland is bare rock and a large snake in the open. Namaris is the phase in which the chaparral's cell is firestorm; Saelura's is spring resurgence, when the scrub comes back thickest.
*Reversal.* A burn across the highland, executed at the Namaris turn: a phase-scale operation under fire law. Zulwazi lineages do not hold burn rights; the Rangitahu lineages of Koremu do, and lend them, never sell them; the lending is a Concord item and the smoke over Zulwazi grazing is the Concord's perennial item, now on the other side of the table. Identified by Element at Master grade at 22 (fire lines the highland would take; the scrub's whole load) or by Life at Master grade (the python needs the scrub; the scrub's health is its own) — either alone gives the fuel or the need, not the operation; a Join of the two at 22 + 22 gives the burn plan. The last act is the burn: the party holds the fire line against the wind for a scene while the python, which feels the inversion, comes out.
*After.* A Master block on bare rock, Guard 15, Vigor 32, no regaining, no concealment, no Surprise. It fights at the town's edge, because that is where the last cover is.
*Layers.* Element (Master): every fire line on the highland and the wind's next turn. Life (Master): every living thing on the highland — which is the python and the things that came because of it. Structure (Master): its mass, precise, and where it will be next turn, which the Overlay gives and the eye does not. Field — Ground (Master): every approach to the town from the highland, and that all of them are its. Field — Nerve: it holds. Boundary (Adept): one a phase, five phases, each empty. Intent: nothing here; the town's fear, at the edge of the scrub.
*Records.* The Concord docket: the Kwazira closure, Saelura 1244, renewed Orrivane and Namaris, lapsing at the Threnis turn unless renewed; the lending of burn rights, proposed by the Kwazira speaker, objected to by the drove-line lineages downwind, deferred. The Tinwara returns: Kwazira hides absent two phases running, cause not recorded. The Watch: the highland reading at Master since 1243, the highest on the map after Awanui, and the Mwamba entry of 1186 beside it.

### 3.6 Oasira — Umutu · Gold Crown · Savanna, Desert, Grassland

Azelra (desert well town), Tinwara (savanna caravan crossroads), Marendi (grassland market town). Ceiling Adept. Ethos: Devout, over well law. The parish files a beast as stock lost and tithes the remainder; the keeper lineages file nothing and count what the well remembers; on truce ground at Tinwara and Marendi no instrument is drawn, which includes a spear, and a beast on truce ground is a problem the truce renewal reads aloud. The Accord creditors who hold sold well ground since 1228 count from a third ledger.

**Tinwara burnt-ground ostriches, Namaris 1244** — Novice · ostrich (a flock of twenty) · Savanna × Namaris: grass fire · node Adept-active (Watch) · Devout ground.
*Ecology.* A flock that runs the grass-fire fronts of the Tinwara circuit and has run through the crossroads market twice. Sign: dust in a straight line ahead of smoke.
*Block.* Run as a Squad Line (Cohesion 6, Guard 12, attack d20 + 3, damage d10 + 1, Move 14). *Amplified trait:* the kick — a member's hit throws its target Prone; the flock's Move is 14 and it does not slow for anything it can go over.
*Rigidity.* Runs in straight lines from the fire and turns only at an angle it cannot go over. *Exploit:* an angled fence; the market's thorn-fence turned across the circuit road at a slant sends the flock past the stalls, a morning's work by the truce ground's keepers.
*Layers.* Element (Novice): fire behind it. Field — Geometry: the line is straight; the corridor is wherever the line points.
*Records.* The parish's stall-damage roll, tithed against. The market keepers' count: twice, and the fence went up the second time.

**Azelra well-scorpions, Saelura 1244** — Novice · scorpion (a population in the well works) · Desert × Saelura: oasis stabilization · node Adept-active (Watch) · Devout ground.
*Ecology.* The stabilized well's lining stones and windlass housing filled with scorpions in Saelura; the give-back laborers are stung at the rate of three a day. Sign: the windlass rope stiff with them.
*Block.* Small; run a disturbed nest as a Squad Line (Cohesion 6, Guard 14, attack d20 + 3, damage d4 + Poisoned, Move 4). *Amplified trait:* the venom — Poisoned: d4 at the start of each turn until a Reserve check at 13, or a Novice purgative.
*Rigidity.* Nests only in the lining stones and the housing, and returns to them after every disturbance. *Exploit:* re-line the well, which is give-back labor and is the keeper lineage's to schedule; a day's work with the stones lifted and smoked, in Saelura, when the water holds and the work keeps. The parish sacrist has offered a rite instead, and the keeper has said the well remembers days, not rites.
*Layers.* Life (Novice): many, well. Field — Seams: the lining stone that lifts. Make: nothing here — no one dosed the well, which the Warlock will confirm and the parish will want in writing.
*Records.* The keeper's well-ledger: stings, in labor-days lost to the well. The parish roll: no entry; a sting is not stock.

**Marendi wildfire-bull, Namaris 1244** — Novice · cape buffalo, bull · Grassland × Namaris: wildfire front · node Adept-active (Watch) · Devout ground.
*Ecology.* A bull that charges out of the wildfire smoke-line at the market's edge at the largest light it sees; it has killed a drover and broken the market's fire. Sign: a buffalo standing in smoke with its head down.
*Block.* Large: Guard 12 · Vigor 22 · attack +1 + d4 · horn d10 + 1 + Rank Die · Move 12 in a charge. *Amplified trait:* the charge — Move 12 in a straight line and its horn deals +Rank Die on a charge; it ignores Burning.
*Rigidity.* Charges the largest fire or light in view, every time. *Exploit:* a decoy fire; a bonfire lit a hundred paces from the market pulls the charge into open ground where a Warden on *Watch* takes it as it comes. On truce ground the market cannot spear it; a hundred paces off is not truce ground, and the truce renewal has read both facts aloud.
*Layers.* Element (Novice): fire behind it, and which light it is looking at. Field — Weight: it commits, to the light. Life: burns on the flank, healing.
*Records.* The parish roll: one drover. The market's truce ledger: the fire broken, relit, and the bull's name in the reading, which is "the bull."

**Tinwara truce-lion, Threnis 1244** — Novice · lion, old male · Savanna × Threnis: pride dominance · node Adept-active (Watch) · Devout ground.
*Ecology.* An old male without a pride that has taken the truce fire's edge as its ground; it comes to the fire at night and eats from the market's slaughter refuse, and no one on truce ground may draw on it. Sign: a lion lying at the edge of the firelight, and a market feeding it.
*Block.* Large: Guard 12 · Vigor 20 · attack +1 + d4 · bite d10 + 1 + Rank Die · Move 10. *Amplified trait:* presence — anyone who comes within 10 paces of it without the market's slaughter refuse in hand is Frightened on a Reserve check at 10.
*Rigidity.* Only the truce fire, only at night, only the refuse; it has never taken stock. *Exploit:* feed it at one fire, which is market truce done as it is done; or wait — it is old. The parish has asked a Zulwazi speaker, at the truce renewal, whether a lion is a claimant. The renewal's record notes the asking.
*Layers.* Life (Novice): old; a tooth gone; well fed. Field — Nerve: holds, at the fire. Intent: nothing here; the market's calm, which is not the lion's.
*Records.* The truce renewal, Threnis 1244, which read the lion aloud after the Standstill and before the fence. The parish roll: a nuisance, untithed.

**Azelra storm-oryx, Namaris 1244** — Adept · oryx (a herd of some thirty) · Desert × Namaris: sandstorms · node Adept-active (Watch) · Devout ground.
*Ecology.* A herd that walks inside its own sandstorm along the pilgrimage road to Azelra, and grazes a salt-bush wadi that Namaris touched; a pilgrim party lost the road inside it for two days. Sign: a storm that moves at a walking pace against the wind.
*Block.* Run as a Squad Line (Cohesion 6, Guard 12, attack d20 + 3, damage d10 + 1, Move 10). *Enhancement:* within 30 paces of the herd a sandstorm stands — concealment for all; ranged attacks and Notice at Hindrance; unprotected eyes take 1 a turn; a Field — Ground reading is the only bearing.
*Dependency.* The salt-bush of one wadi, which the herd grazes and returns to; the storm is what the bush does to the air the herd breathes. Found by Life at Adept grade by contact with a carcass or a browsed bush (what it needs: this bush, from this wadi) or by Element (air answers at the wadi and not on the open road).
*Disruption.* Graze it out — a keeper lineage's cattle turned into the wadi for a phase, which the parish would call trespass on shrine ground and the lineage would call grazing; or Elemental *Shape* (ground) at 16, four casts, to bury the bush line; or Nature *Quiet* on the herd's lead, held a scene, which stops the herd and not the storm.
*After.* Oryx on a wadi, which the pilgrims count as a sight of the road.
*Layers.* Life (Adept): the bush, from the wadi. Element (Adept): air answers at the wadi. Field — Ground: the road, at Hindrance, and the herd's line, exact. Boundary: none.
*Records.* The parish's pilgrimage-road losses on the Tinwara circuit, in tithe not collected. The herders' count: thirty head, one bull, and the wadi's name, which the parish does not have.

**Marendi recovery-mounds, Saelura 1244** — Adept · termite (a colony) · Grassland × Saelura: soil recovery · node Adept-active (Watch) · Devout ground.
*Ecology.* A colony whose mounds spread across the recovered market grassland and regrow overnight; the stall ground is a mound-field, and the sold ground beside it, which a creditor holds, is not. Sign: mounds where stalls were, and a surveyor's stakes standing among them.
*Block.* Soldiers, if a mound is broken: a Squad Line (Cohesion 6, Guard 12, attack d20 + 3, damage d6, Move 4). *Enhancement:* the mounds regrow to full height at the start of each night; the mound-field is difficult ground — Move halved, and any Line crossing it makes a Cohesion check at 13 — and a mound breached is a mound rebuilt by morning.
*Dependency.* The queen chamber under the oldest mound, whose reading is a mass where the map has grassland. Found by Structure at Adept grade (a mass, deep, where there should be none; precise) or by the creditor's survey, which has staked something it calls a rock.
*Disruption.* Arcane *Precise Force* on the chamber's roof at 16, three successes; or dig it out — a day's work with twelve laborers at Frame 16, under soldiers. The creditor has offered to pay for the digging on the condition that the ground surveyed clear is entered as his; the parish and the keeper lineage have, for once, agreed on an answer.
*After.* Termites, which the grassland has always had.
*Layers.* Structure (Adept): the chamber, deep, precise. Life (Adept): the colony's health, which is the soil's. Field — Seams: where a mound breaks, which is at the base on the shaded side. Make: nothing here.
*Records.* The creditor's survey (Accord, in seals). The parish's stall roll (in gilts). The keeper's ledger: the ground is a well's catchment and always was.

**Tinwara reversed gazelles, Orrivane 1244** — Adept · gazelle (a herd of sixty) · Savanna × Orrivane: migration reversal · node Adept-active (Watch) · Devout ground.
*Ecology.* A herd running the Namaris circuit backwards, against the tithe collectors' route, and circling the crossroads' waymark stone; inside its run the collectors cannot keep their road. Sign: gazelles running the wrong way round a stone, and a Tithe collector walking in a circle.
*Block.* Run as a Squad Line (Cohesion 6, Guard 13, attack d20 + 3, damage d8, Move 14). *Enhancement:* within 30 paces of the herd's run, Notice to hold a bearing is at Difficulty 19 and mounts bolt on a Reserve check at 13; anyone who moves without a Field — Ground reading held moves the way the herd runs.
*Dependency.* The crossroads' waymark stone, which the caravan houses set and whose reading drifts. Found by Structure at Adept grade (the stone's position is not the survey's and moves a pace a reading) or by the houses' mile-book, which has re-measured the crossroads three times this year.
*Disruption.* Move the stone — a cart and four men, Frame 16, half a day; or Arcane *Precise Force* on its base at 16; or *Brace* it held a scene, which stops the drift and the herd for as long as the Brace is paid.
*After.* Gazelles at a crossroads, going whichever way the season says.
*Layers.* Structure (Adept): the stone moved a pace. Field — Ground: the road, and that the herd's line is not it. Life: sixty, well.
*Records.* The Tithe's circuit log: two collections missed. The houses' mile-book: the crossroads re-surveyed three times; the third survey signed by the surveyor's mark and no seal, which the Ledger has queried.

### 3.7 Koremu — Tangata · Green Chimera · Tropical Rainforest, Grassland, Desert

Motuweka (rainforest river settlement), Rangitahu (grassland fire country), Onekura (red-sand desert edge). Ceiling Master, at Lake Marama and the fire country. Ethos: Reverie, under way law and fire law. A beast on a way is a matter for the way's keeper; a keeper may close the way by declaration, and the closure lapses at the phase turn unless renewed. Nothing is reported to the Ledger, which estimates Koremu from the way-tolls the Meridian pays. No Master rolled; the Marama entry of 1091 is the ceiling's reason and the keepers have not let the Watch back.

**Motuweka moth-crossing, Orrivane 1244** — Novice · moth (a swarm) · Rainforest × Orrivane: swarm disorientation · node Adept-active (Watch, from the road) · Reverie ground.
*Ecology.* A swarm that rises at dusk from the far bank and crosses the river at the settlement's landing; inside it lanterns show nothing and a canoe turns. Sign: the far bank going grey at dusk, and the landing's lamps lit and useless.
